transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-17 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Kaur (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (Head of ML, Citrine), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Jordan Lee (Product), Sam Carter (Security)

Auto-summary (auto):
Redwood walked through Evaluation/Quality monitoring features in the Console and Optimize: how to construct prompt sets, set regression alerts, and run A/B comparisons. Customer asked about data residency, private deployments, and how alerts map to SLAs.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Samir from our solutions team will walk through the Eval features.
[00:15] Alex (Head of ML): Hey, Alex here. We're excited — we want to stop regressions sneaking into prod.
[00:30] Samir (SE): Cool, quick agenda: prompt-sets, baseline evaluation, regression alerts, and A/B compare flows in Redwood Console and Redwood Optimize. We'll demo a small prompt set and show alert thresholds.
[00:45] Priya (Platform): Side question — can we run this in our VPC? We have strict data residency rules.
[00:55] Samir (SE): Yes. Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem. For hosted, we have configurable retention and encryption. We'll send our KMS/HSM docs in the security pack.
[01:10] Jordan (Product): How noisy are the alerts? We want signal not noise.
[01:20] Samir (SE): Great question. Alerts are tied to score deltas over chosen windows and you can tune sensitivity per prompt-set or per intent. We also support pairwise comparisons and human-in-the-loop triage for noisy signals.
[01:40] Maya (AE): Quick qualification — what's your current stack? models, infra?
[01:50] Alex (Head of ML): We're on a mix: model hosting with a managed provider now, some internal quantized models for latency-critical flows. Most inference is via API. We use SSO via Okta and KMS via AWS.
[02:10] Samir (SE): That maps well. On the Console you'll see we version prompt-sets, attach success metrics (like BLEU-ish or custom scalar), and create regression rules. I'll share an example: if median score drops 5% over 24 hours, alert.
[02:35] Evan (SE): Note: our KV cache and prefix caching can reduce cost in the steady state — sometimes a few words get transcribed as K V cash in transcripts so just flagging that happens in speech exports.
[02:55] Priya (Platform): Pricing question — how does cost look for running continuous eval? We'll have a lot of requests.
[03:05] Maya (AE): Two levers: sampling rate (how many prompts you run) and batching/quantization recommendations from Optimize. For pilot we suggest sampling 200 prompts daily to balance cost and coverage. We'll give a cost estimate in the pricing follow-up.
[03:25] Alex (Head of ML): For A/B comparisons, do you support traffic splits and drift-aware comparisons?
[03:35] Samir (SE): Yes. You can define splits (e.g., 50/50), store per-variant metrics, and use paired significance tests over your prompt-set. We also annotate prompts with metadata (intent, priority) to slice results.
[03:55] Jordan (Product): Can we attach custom eval functions? Like run an LLM-based rubric on the outputs?
[04:05] Samir (SE): You can plug in custom evaluators. We support JS/Python eval hooks in the Eval pipeline or call out to a hosted function. We'll demo a small JS rubric now.
[04:30] [DEMO START] Samir (SE): Opening the Console — here's the Eval section. Create new prompt-set -> import CSV or paste prompts. You can tag prompts, set expected output and scoring function.
[05:00] Samir (SE): Importing a sample 20-prompt CSV I prepared. Note the mismatch tolerance and normalized score. Sometimes the auto-transcribed examples will show weird punctuation; ignore that for now.
[05:30] Alex (Head of ML): If we want to detect hallucination rate change, can we add a binary classifier eval?
[05:40] Samir (SE): Yep; add a classifier eval or integrate your internal classifier as a custom evaluator. Alerts can be fired on any metric.
[06:05] Priya (Platform): About compliance: SOC2, audit logs, RBAC?
[06:15] Maya (AE): We have SOC2 Type II for the hosted product, and Private deployments keep logs in your VPC. RBAC and SSO via SAML/Okta are supported. We'll include our audit-log sample and a short note on retention policy in the pack.
[06:40] Samir (SE): Back to A/B — here's the compare UI: choose baseline, variant, metric, and time window. You can define canary rules to gradually ramp. We also surface a confidence interval and p-value.
[07:05] Evan (SE): Quick caveat — when comparing small sample sizes, we'll show warnings. Best practice is run at least several hundred prompts per variant or use paired tests on the same prompts.
[07:30] Jordan (Product): On rollout, if variant fails, can we automatically rollback?
[07:40] Samir (SE): Yes; our rollouts support automatic fallback policies. For Dedicated/Private, that's configured at the routing layer.
[08:00] Alex (Head of ML): For our pilot, timeline wise, we want a 4-week pilot then decide on Dedicated. What's typical?
[08:10] Maya (AE): Typical pilot is 2–6 weeks: setup, ingest prompts, run bench, evaluate. We'll help set success criteria and a post-pilot readout.
[08:30] Priya (Platform): Data residency — if we use hosted, can we limit region? We need EU-only for some data.
[08:40] Maya (AE): Yes, regional pinning is supported for hosted; for stricter needs Private deployment recommended. We'll document regional options.
[09:00] [DEMO - ALERTS] Samir (SE): Creating a regression alert: choose dataset, metric, baseline period, threshold. Example: if average helpfulness score drops by 7% vs rolling 7-day baseline, send Slack + email and open an incident. You can tune debounce windows to reduce noise.
[09:35] Alex (Head of ML): How are false positives handled? We don't want pages at 2am for minor variance.
[09:45] Samir (SE): Use multi-tier alerts: warning (email), critical (pager). Also configure suppression windows and human review step before paging.
[10:10] Jordan (Product): Does Console support attaching sample failing outputs to alerts?
[10:20] Samir (SE): Yes, alerts can include top failing examples and links to the eval run. That makes triage faster.
[10:45] Priya (Platform): Any concerns about PII in these samples?
[10:55] Maya (AE): We mask or obfuscate by default in hosted logs; for Private you control retention and masking policies. We'll include our data handling note.
[11:15] Alex (Head of ML): Ok, looks promising. For the A/B plan — we want to test two prompt families and a quantized model variant. Can Redwood do multi-variant compare?
[11:30] Samir (SE): Yes. We support up to N-way comparisons and generate pairwise reports. For quantized variants, we also surface latency and cost delta per-token.
[11:55] Evan (SE): One demo note: sometimes transcripts show 'K B cache' instead of 'KV cache' — not important but happens in auto-transcript.
[12:10] Jordan (Product): What's the onboarding effort for our team?
[12:20] Maya (AE): For a pilot, typically 2–3 Redwood touchpoints: kickoff, data ingestion assist, bench run. We also provide a quickstart repo and prompt-set templates.
[12:40] Alex (Head of ML): Regarding SSO and RBAC, Sam, can you walk Sam Carter (security) through the audit logs next week?
[12:50] Samir (SE): Yep, happy to; let's schedule a security review.
[13:05] Sam Carter (Security): We'll want encryption-at-rest proof and KMS integration details.
[13:15] Maya (AE): We'll include KMS/HSM notes and a contact for our security engineer in the pack.
[13:30] [CROSS-TALK] Alex: Also — can we export results as CSV for our internal dashboards?
[13:40] Samir (SE): Yes, exportable CSVs and API access to eval results.
[13:55] Jordan: For the pilot success metric — we want <=2% degradation in overall helpfulness and no increase in hallucination rate.
[14:05] Maya: Noted. We'll help instrument those metrics.
[14:20] [WRAP-UP] Maya (AE): Recap: we'll send security pack and SOC2 summary, Samir will send prompt-set templates and A/B checklist, customer to provide 200 prompts and success criteria by next week, and we'll schedule bench run for week of 2025-04-28.
[14:45] Alex: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[14:50] Priya: Appreciate the demo.
[15:00] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and the links.
